issues.description: The problem statement (text and UML) declares acceptSupplyDelivery as taking four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity), but both the provided template usage and the reference solution implement and call acceptSupplyDelivery with only three parameters (ingredient name, price, quantity). This mismatch can confuse students about the required method signature and lead to implementations that don't match the tests or the provided code examples.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the acceptSupplyDelivery signature consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement and UML to specify acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) (removing the supplier parameter), or (B) change the template Main and the solution to use a four-parameter signature (e.g., acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplier, String name, int price, int quantity)) and adjust all calls accordingly. Preferably align the problem text/UML with the actual intended 3-parameter API to match the template and tests.

issues.description: The problem statement's API for acceptSupplyDelivery describes a four-parameter signature (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity) in the UML/text, while the provided template and the solution code use a three-parameter signature (ingredient name, price, quantity). This mismatch in the method signature (and parameter roles) creates an unclear mapping for students: they may try to implement or call acceptSupplyDelivery with four parameters as described in the problem, but the starter code and reference solution expect three. The conceptual entity (the supply-delivery API) is therefore represented with inconsistent parameter lists across artifacts.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the acceptSupplyDelivery API across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement to specify the three-parameter signature used by the template and solution: acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity), or (B) update the template and solution to implement the four-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and adjust all calls (e.g., in Main) accordingly. Prefer option A if the supplier name is not used in logic, to minimize changes.
